messages:
jessie: heads-up — my feature branch `ui/streaming-metrics` started failing CI after i rebased onto main. local `pytest tests/metrics -q` passes. CI is failing two tests: `tests/metrics/test_streaming.py::test_buffer_flush` and `tests/e2e/test_streaming_end_to_end.py::test_backpressure`. build: https://ci.internal.redwood/builds/5532

jessie: failing snippet from the CI log:
```
E   AssertionError: Expected 32 got 0
tests/metrics/test_streaming.py:47: AssertionError
--- logs ---
TimeoutError: Process timed out after 30s
Sequence ended prematurely
```

Mohit: did the rebase include any infra/docker changes? sometimes image tags drift and CI uses a different base. also, did you rebase merges from infra/main?

jessie: i only rebased on origin/main. here's the commit range: `git log --oneline origin/main..HEAD` -> `def5678 add streaming backpressure fix`
`abc1234 tweak metrics flush timing`

Tia: could be a race that only shows up under the CI concurrency profile. two quick checks: 1) can you run the failing tests 50-100x locally (pytest-repeat) inside the same docker image CI uses? 2) try rerunning CI with cache/artifacts disabled (sometimes stale cached state triggers timeouts).

Oliver: I can trigger a no-cache run if you add a comment on the PR with `[rerun-no-cache]` or ping me. also, is the CI runner using the same Python runtime/docker tag as your laptop? mismatched asyncio loop implementations (uvloop vs default) have bitten us before.

CI Bot: :x: Build 5532 failed on branch `ui/streaming-metrics` — see https://ci.internal.redwood/builds/5532/logs

jessie: ran `docker run --rm -it redwood/collector:2026-03-10-7f1a pytest tests/metrics/test_streaming.py::test_buffer_flush -q --count=100` — all 100 passed locally in the container image that matches my local dev env. so i think it's CI-specific timing / env.

Tia: ok that's useful. next step: try to reproduce CI conditions locally: run with parallel workers (xdist) and simulate e2e load, or add a short instrumentation in the test to log buffer sizes and timestamps. if we can reproduce flake locally we can bisect.

Mohit: if you want i can start a git bisect across the two suspected commits on a CI node (slow but isolates culprit). ping me the SHAs to bisect between.

jessie: thanks — bisect range `abc1234..def5678`. i'll add some debug prints to the test and then request a no-cache rerun. if it still fails i'll ask you to kick off the bisect, @Mohit. :thumbsup:

Oliver: also double-check that the CI runner has the same env vars, especially `STREAM_BUFFER_SIZE` and `REDWOOD_TEST_MODE`. those envs changed in a recent infra patch and could affect flushing logic.

jessie: good call — envs look the same from the build artifact, but i'll explicitly set them in the pipeline for the rerun. thanks all, i'll update here once i have results. :pray:
